systemsMapSummary: The trial is a team product that begins as a single-player experience. A team lead signs up, works through a 7-step workspace-setup wizard alone, and creates a first project (54% do). But the value of the product only appears once the team is inside it — and three things quietly block that. First, nothing in the product prompts an invite after the first project is created, so setup ends solo and the account stays a party of one (71% never invite anyone). Second, imported cards from spreadsheets or Trello are hard to find again, which erodes trust at exactly the moment a lead would show the tool to colleagues. Third, because the trial is quiet in week one, there is no reason to return before it lapses. These reinforce each other: solo setup means no teammates, no teammates means no shared board (only 22% reach one), and no shared board means the collaborative value never lands — so conversion sits at 6.0%. The highest-leverage moment is right after the first project is created, while intent is fresh.

topLeveragePoints.point: Prompt a teammate invite at the moment the first project is created
topLeveragePoints.currentState: There is no in-product prompt to invite after the first project; setup ends solo and 71% never invite.

topLeveragePoints.point: Make imported cards from spreadsheets or Trello easy to find after migration
topLeveragePoints.currentState: 'Where did my imported cards go?' is a top support theme; lost work breaks trust early.

topLeveragePoints.point: Give the team lead a reason to return within the first 48 hours
topLeveragePoints.currentState: The trial is 'too quiet' in week one; nothing pulls the lead back before it goes cold.

headline: If we turned solo setup into a team invite at the first-project moment, we'd likely see activation move from 22% toward the target and conversion rise from 6.0% without discounting.
